title: Culture or Superstition? India’s Heritage Questioned
description:
India is often celebrated as a land of culture and heritage — but how much of it is really just superstition? From avoiding non-veg on certain days, to cricket match rituals, astrology, vastu, ayurveda, lemon-chili charms, evil eye, palmistry, numerology, godmen, milk-drinking idols, witch hunts, and “auspicious” muhurats — our so-called traditions are soaked in irrational beliefs.

In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts asks a bold question: is there anything in our culture and heritage that is not bound to superstition? From everyday habits to national practices, superstition disguises itself as “belief” or “heritage.” Surveys even show that scientists and workplaces in India are not immune to pseudoscience — astrology courses in universities, vaastu at offices, Tirupati blessings before rocket launches.

Science, in contrast, is humble enough to admit what it doesn’t know. Instead of glorifying blind traditions, Article 51A(h) of our Constitution asks us to practice scientific temper, humanism, and inquiry. This video challenges the glorification of irrational practices and calls for a generation that can separate culture worth preserving from superstition that must be discarded.

If you’ve searched for “Indian superstitions explained,” “culture vs superstition,” “astrology vaastu debunked,” “why India is superstitious,” “superstition in workplace,” or “scientific temper constitution”, this video questions what we proudly call heritage. Don’t forget to like, share, and subscribe to support reason over ritual.
